article: PaperModの記事一覧の画像配置
scope: Rewrote the Japanese article and twelve translations against PaperMod's official FAQ and current upstream post-entry stylesheet. Compared the legacy CSS/template instructions, selectors, HTML assumptions, responsive behavior, language alignment, links, and publication metadata.
findings: Removed duplicated conflicting future dates, preserved the original 2022-09-11 publication date, and added lastmod 2026-11-24 in every locale.
Replaced instructions to edit bundled blank.css and post-entry.css with PaperMod's supported assets/css/extended/custom.css approach.
Corrected the ineffective instruction to delete a commented-out width declaration; removing the comment would not change CSS behavior.
Replaced brittle inline-flex/template edits and incomplete line-clamp rules with a responsive CSS Grid layout using PaperMod's current post-entry classes.
Clarified that the snippet changes list-card covers, not images inside article content, and added browser checks for narrow screens and full-card links.
Aligned the Japanese article, twelve translations, and identical code sample; replaced stale instructions with official current references.

post/PaperModの画像の配置変更/index.ar.md.summary: Rewrote and checked against the Japanese source, current PaperMod FAQ and its upstream post-entry CSS; aligned all locale text and the shared responsive CSS Grid example.

meaning.note: Aligned the target (post-list cover cards), extension-CSS workflow, CSS Grid behavior, responsive adjustment, and distinction from article-body images.

terminology.note: Checked PaperMod, extended CSS, post-entry, entry-cover, grid areas, breakpoint, theme override, and responsive terminology.

mathematics.note: The example uses an illustrative 150px desktop column and 96px narrow-screen column; neither is a factual or mathematical claim.

code.note: Compared the exact shared CSS across locales; confirmed it targets current documented PaperMod classes, keeps image height automatic, and avoids editing bundled theme files or relying on a commented-out declaration.

links.note: Added PaperMod's official FAQ and upstream stylesheet, plus the original discussion for context.

limitations: AI-assisted review; no human or native-speaker certification.
The CSS relies on PaperMod's current post-list classes; theme updates or forks may change the markup, so verify in a browser.
